verdicts.quote: All-or-nothing: if anything in the file is invalid or conflicts, no user is created and every problem is reported at once. Chosen over per-row partial creation
every row is checked, and all problems are returned in one response ... `row_errors` 422 with `total`, `invalid`, `created=0` and one entry per bad row.
an email that already belongs to a user is an error, never an update or skip. ... A row is `duplicate_in_file` when an earlier row has the same email
The CSV carries no password and no role. Imported users get the same default role and initial state as a user made through single-create. ... a role column is a privilege-escalation path.
the import is available only to an authenticated user who holds the administrator role at the moment the request is processed.
verdicts.missing: Whether import is a distinct permission from single-user create, i.e. that being able to create one user does not by itself grant bulk import.

verdicts.quote: a header row. Header names are trimmed and case-insensitive; exactly `email` and `name`, each once, in any order, and no other column.
UTF-8 (an optional leading BOM is ignored), comma-delimited, with LF or CRLF line ends, quoted fields per RFC 4180 (commas, doubled quotes and line breaks inside quotes)
effects that leave the system ... happen only after the whole import has been durably committed, and never for users of a rejected import. A failure of such an effect does not undo any user
at `IMPORT_MAX_BYTES` accepted, one byte over refused; at `IMPORT_MAX_ROWS` accepted, one row over refused.
verdicts.missing: The actual byte and row limit values; G-5 leaves them as configuration with no default.

verdicts.quote: FX-8a / 8b / 8c | zero bytes / `email,name\n` only / ... | `empty_file` / `no_rows` / valid with 1 row
The same file submitted twice is not a special case: the second submission finds every email taken.
The import runs synchronously in one request, bounded by configured row and byte limits (G-5). No numeric bound is invented here; a larger scale would need an asynchronous design
verdicts.missing: No background processing or completion notification is specified; whether large files are supported depends on undecided limits and a deferred async redesign.

verdicts.quote: exactly one message is queued per created user, none before the commit ... delivery is asynchronous and owned by the existing mechanism
verdicts.missing: Whether hundreds of messages may go out at once and any pacing or throttling of them.

verdicts.quote: an imported user is indistinguishable from one made through single-create in role, initial state and effects ... No password is read from or written to the file
verdicts.missing: The actual initial state (active/pending) and first sign-in method; deferred to G-2/G-4.

verdicts.quote: The uploaded bytes live only for the request and any temporary copy is removed when the request ends, on success, failure or client disconnect.
each import attempt by an authenticated user writes one audit record: actor, time, sanitised file name, total rows if known, created count, outcome
a corrected file can be re-uploaded whole ... no durable import record or resume is provided (A-8) because the all-or-nothing rule makes a resume unnecessary.
verdicts.missing: Whether and how a running import can be cancelled.

verdicts.missing: A concrete time bound for a maximum-size file and any visible progress beyond a busy indicator.
